correctness.rationale: The left-to-right prefix search rejects exactly repeated forward displacement differences for each h; every valid Costas permutation survives, so exhaustion is genuine and not partial raw enumeration. The original left-to-right hash-based and reverse-bitmask/direct-retest checkers were inspected. A separate independently written exhaustive C++ implementation generated all valid permutations and directly retested the full Costas predicate after each swap: n=11 4368 vertices, 140 edges, deg0/1/2=4096/264/8; n=12 7852 vertices 136 edges 7580 K1 +136 K2 gaps (8,16,4,0,20,40,8,8,20,8,4); n=13 12828 vertices 88 edges 12652 K1 +88 K2 gaps (12,16,8,4,12,4,8,0,0,8,8,8); n=14 17252 vertices 120 edges 17012 K1 +120 K2 gaps (12,0,20,0,0,8,8,0,12,12,32,12,4). Reverse enumeration is independent by different recursion; matching degree hist and gaps certify exact finite target instances, not an all-n theorem.

value.rationale: A natural legal-swap reconfiguration graph for Costas arrays has a sharp finite immobility phenomenon: n=11 admits eight degree-two states, but n=12..14 are matchings so no two-step walk visits a third array. The new complete degree/gap refinement is mathematically motivated by connectivity and local search obstacles, not a raw re-tabulation of already known aggregate pair totals.

limitations: Only n=12,13,14; no statement for n>=15.
